title: spatial-temporal-threshold-sweep
content:
Goal: quick exploratory sweep to find the spatial (cache hit distribution across user prefixes) and temporal (idle-to-burst warmup) thresholds where we start seeing >2x p99 pain for small requests. Aim is to inform adaptive prefetch + batching heuristics.

Context / why:
- Recent customer incident (RD-2147) saw p99 spikes when a small cohort hit after 45–90s idle windows. Hypothesis: KV cache eviction by LRU + shard hot-reshuffle before steady multiplexing.
- Want to quantify where simple prefix prewarm (width X) buys us latency and where it becomes wasteful for throughput.

Environment / harness:
- Model: gomel-7B-fp16 (prod-sim variant)
- Hardware: single A100-80GB (shared dev pool), isolated runtime instance
- Runtime config: kv_cache=True, cache_capacity=256MB, batcher.max_batch_tokens=2048
- Client: local loader that simulates arrival patterns; measures end-to-end server response start-to-last-byte
- Measurement slice: token-length requests with prompt=short (avg 24 tokens), gen cap=16 tokens

Sweep plan (coarse first pass):
- Spatial prewarm width W: [1, 4, 8, 16]
- Temporal idle interval I: [5s, 20s, 45s, 90s, 180s]
- Concurrent inflight (fanout) levels C: [1, 4, 8]
- 3 repeats per cell, 2-minute steady-state after start, collect per-request latency plus timestamps

Notes on workload generator:
- Arrival shape: burst (all requests at t=0 for 2s) and spaced (poisson lambda to match QPS 30)
- For burst we measure initial 30s post-burst heavily since warmup effects show then
- We capture kernel-level metrics via /metrics endpoint (kv_hits, batch_size_histogram, cpu_gpu_util)

Representative raw results (median of repeats) — burst mode, C=4, prompt 24 tokens:
W=1, I=45s => QPS_peak 110, median_latency 78ms, p95 240ms, p99 620ms, kv_hit_rate 12%
W=4, I=45s => QPS_peak 108, median_latency 82ms, p95 160ms, p99 220ms, kv_hit_rate 41%
W=8, I=45s => QPS_peak 103, median_latency 84ms, p95 150ms, p99 190ms, kv_hit_rate 58%
W=16, I=45s => QPS_peak 101, median_latency 86ms, p95 148ms, p99 185ms, kv_hit_rate 67%

Trend calls:
- Doubling W from 1->4 yielded ~3x reduction in p99 for the 45s idle case while throughput dropped only ~2%.
- Marginal returns after W=8 are small for p99; cost (memory + increased prefetching) grows.
- For short idle (I=5s) effect is muted: W=1 already had kv_hit_rate ~65% and p99 ~95ms.

Edge case (I=180s, burst):
W=1 => p99 950ms, kv_hit 4%
W=4 => p99 540ms, kv_hit 22%
W=8 => p99 250ms, kv_hit 48%
=> indicates large idle windows need wider prewarm to avoid catastrophic slowdown. But note that prewarming W=8 at I=180s increases background prefetch work that will collide with other tenants in multi-tenant pool.

Observed failure modes / anomalies:
- One repeat at W=16, I=90s had GPU stall 3s (rare) — kernel-level logs show a cuBLAS allocation panic then recovery; filing infra PR (see linked PR).
- Batch size histogram during warmups showed many single-request batches (batch_size=1) for first 12s; batching config had conservative timeout=5ms which may be too low for noisy bursts.

Quick ascii heatmap (p99 ms by W x I) — rough
(I cols: 5s,20s,45s,90s,180s)
W=1 | 95, 120, 620, 780, 950
W=4 | 90, 110, 220, 310, 540
W=8 | 88, 105, 190, 210, 250
W=16| 85, 102, 185, 200, 220

Preliminary conclusions (for discussion):
1) For customer-facing default, recommend a conservative W=4 prewarm when idle>30s for hosted pool; gives good p99 improvement with modest cost. Tag as opt-in configurable by tenant.
2) For Dedicated/private where memory isolation exists, suggest W=8 as a default for aggressive low-p99 SLAs.
3) Batching timeout needs re-evaluation: increase to 8–12ms during detected warmup windows to allow small coalescing and avoid 1-shot batches.
4) Add circuit to detect repeated long-idle accesses (I>60s) and trigger selective cold-warm prefetch only for heavy prefixes (top-K by recent QPS) — to cap background cost.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Expand sweep to multi-GPU small pool (2xA100) to measure cross-shard KV coherence cost (assign to Jordan)
- Add a measurement for tail-queueing: capture queue length at APIGW when burst hits (Maya)
- Draft a short customer note template explaining mitigation options (so we can proactively contact impacted customers)
- Create rollout flag "prefetch-width" with server-side default 4 and per-tenant override; add canary (RD-2189)

Questions to answer in follow-up runs:
- How does prewarm width interact with quantized model variants (int8) — less memory, different kernel shapes
- Is there a smarter LRU variant (freq-aware) that keeps prefixes seen in the last 5 minutes irrespective of raw recency?

Notes to self:
- Save raw traces to s3://redwood-dev/sofia/spatial-sweep/2025-01-17/ (done)
- Re-run the failing W=16 case with env var RTF_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 to catch GPU allocation sequences
- Check the PR tests against prod-kernel-compat matrix

Rough estimate of unit cost impact (back of envelope):
- W=4 prewarm adds ~+6% avg memory footprint, increases background token generation ~0.8 tokens/sec per prewarm width per instance during idle windows.
- For hosted at scale we need a throttling limiter to avoid >10% baseline cost uplift when many tenants idle concurrently.

If anyone wants the raw csv per-run ping me and I'll share. Slack: @sofia.martins.

End of scratchpad.
